chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan narrated to us, he said: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us, he said: Hassan ibn Ali al-Mada'ini narrated to us, he said: Al-Abbas ibn Makram narrated to us, from Sa'd al-Khaffaf, from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said: Uthman ibn Affan wrote, when he was surrounded, to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him): To proceed,

the water has exceeded the zuba, the belt has reached the tubyayn, the matter has exceeded its extent with me, and I have been sought by those who do not repel from themselves. Hence, if you are one who eats, then be the best one who eats. Otherwise, catch up with me while I am being ripped.

key_terms.الزُّبَى: A place or boundary, used idiomatically to mean exceeding limits or reaching a point of no return.
key_terms.الطَّبِيقَيْنِ: The two layers or strata, used idiomatically to mean reaching the core or the highest level.
key_terms.خَيْرَ آكِلٍ: The best eater (idiom for the one who takes control or consumes the matter).

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the idioms 'zuba' and 'tubyayn' in Uthman's letter to Ali?
ai.summary: This letter, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Mani al-Akhbar*, captures the critical moment of Uthman's siege where he invokes Ali's political and spiritual authority to resolve the internal strife (Fitna). The phrase 'Zuba' refers to the point of no return in a journey, symbolizing that the rebellion had surpassed the initial grievances, while 'Tubyayn' alludes to the encirclement of the city, highlighting the urgency for Ali to intervene either to assume leadership or to prevent Uthman's martyrdom.
